# @nivinjoseph/n-domain

> TypeScript framework for Domain-Driven Design with Event Sourcing: event-sourced aggregate roots, domain events, value objects/entities, snapshots, point-in-time reconstruction, rebasing, typeVersion state migrations, and multi-tenant (Org*) variants. ESM only, Node >= 24.10, standard (ES2023+) TypeScript decorators.

Install: `npm install @nivinjoseph/n-domain`

Sibling packages you will touch: `@nivinjoseph/n-util` (Serializable, `@serialize`, Deserializer — the whole serialization mechanism), `@nivinjoseph/n-defensive` (`given(...)` assertions — every runtime contract here throws through it), `@nivinjoseph/n-ext` (prototype extensions, loaded as a side effect of importing this package). `@nivinjoseph/n-eda` is NOT a dependency, but `DomainEvent.refType/refId/partitionKey` exist for compatibility with it — you must implement `refType` regardless.

## Exports

- `AggregateRoot<TState, TDomainEvent>` — abstract event-sourced aggregate base
- `AggregateFactory` — preferred way to instantiate aggregates from events
- `AggregateState` — base state interface (`typeVersion`, `id`, `version`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `isRebased`, `rebasedFromVersion`)
- `AggregateStateFactory<TState>` — abstract factory owning defaults (`create()`), migrations (`update()`), snapshot revival
- `AggregateStateHelper` — static utils: `serializeStateIntoSnapshot`, `deserializeSnapshotIntoState`, `rebaseState`, `fingerprintState` (drift-guard SHA-512)
- `AggregateRootData` — serialized aggregate shape (`$id`, `$version`, `$createdAt`, `$updatedAt`, `$events`)
- `DomainEvent<TState>` — abstract event base; `DomainEventData` — its serialized shape (`$`-prefixed keys)
- `DomainObject<TThis, TDataKeys>` — value object base (structural `equals`); `DomainObjectData<T>` — constructor-input type (nested domain objects are live instances); `DomainObjectSerialized<TThis, TDataKeys>`/`SerializedValue<V>` — `serialize()`'s deep plain-data return type (nested domain objects serialized recursively, `$typename` at every level; not interchangeable with the input type). RULE: anything extending DomainObject (value objects AND entities) serializes correctly only when held directly or in a single-level array — inside `Array<Array<...>>` or plain-object properties they get JSON-mangled at runtime, so those positions type as `never` by design, in BOTH the constructor input (violating classes are unconstructible — `new` does not compile) and the serialized output. Always-legal data shapes: scalars, enums/literal unions, Date (→ ISO string), nullable variants, and plain objects/arrays of these at any depth (with no domain object inside)
- `DomainEntity<TThis, TDataKeys>` — entity base (identity `equals`, structural `deepEquals`)
- `DomainContext` (`{ userId }`), `ConfigurableDomainContext` — context implementations
- `DomainHelper` — `now`, `generateId("abc")` (3-letter prefix, sortable ulid-based), `aggregateTypeToSnakeCase`
- Org* multi-tenant variants: `OrgAggregateRoot`, `OrgAggregateState`, `OrgAggregateStateFactory`, `OrgDomainContext`, `OrgConfigurableDomainContext`, `OrgDomainEvent`, `OrgDomainEventData` — thread `organizationId` through context, state, and events

## Minimal correct skeletons

Value object:

```typescript
@serialize("App")                                                    // namespace REQUIRED
export class TodoDescription extends DomainObject<TodoDescription, "description">
{
    private readonly _description: string;

    @serialize
    public get description(): string { return this._description; }

    public constructor(data: DomainObjectData<TodoDescription>)
    {
        super(data);
        this._description = data.description;
    }
}
```

Abstract per-aggregate event base:

```typescript
export abstract class TodoDomainEvent extends DomainEvent<TodoState>
{
    public get refType(): string { return "Todo"; }                  // string LITERAL, never an import
}
```

Created event:

```typescript
@serialize("App")
export class TodoCreated extends TodoDomainEvent
{
    private readonly _todoId: string;

    @serialize
    public get todoId(): string { return this._todoId; }

    public constructor(data: EventData)
    {
        data.$isCreatedEvent = true;                                  // BEFORE super(data)
        super(data);
        this._todoId = data.todoId;
    }

    protected applyEvent(state: TodoState): void
    {
        state.id = this._todoId;                                      // created event MUST set state.id
    }
}

interface EventData extends DomainEventData { todoId: string; }
```

State + factory:

```typescript
export interface TodoState extends AggregateState { title: string; }

export class TodoStateFactory extends AggregateStateFactory<TodoState>
{
    public create(): TodoState
    {
        return { ...this.createDefaultAggregateState(), title: null as any };   // deterministic!
    }
}
```

Aggregate:

```typescript
@serialize("App")
export class Todo extends AggregateRoot<TodoState, TodoDomainEvent>
{
    public get title(): string { return this.state.title; }

    public static create(domainContext: DomainContext, title: string): Todo
    {
        const createdEvent = new TodoCreated({ todoId: DomainHelper.generateId("tdo"), title });
        return new AggregateFactory(Todo, domainContext, new TodoStateFactory())
            .createFromEvents([createdEvent]);
    }

    public updateTitle(title: string): void
    {
        this.applyEvent(new TodoTitleUpdated({ title }));
    }
}
```

## Rules the type system does not enforce

1. `@serialize("Namespace")` is required on every aggregate class, every concrete event class, and every DomainObject/DomainEntity class, plus bare `@serialize` on each payload getter. Omitting it compiles fine and even persists — then replay/deserialization fails at runtime.
2. In a created event's constructor, assign `data.$isCreatedEvent = true` BEFORE calling `super(data)` (the base constructor reads it). Exactly one created event per stream — zero or two throws.
3. The created event's `applyEvent` must set `state.id`, or apply throws "Created event did not set the id of the aggregate".
4. The event CLASS NAME is the persisted identity (`$name`). Renaming an event class breaks deserialization of every stored stream.
5. `refType` must return a string literal of the aggregate's type name. Never `Todo.getTypeName()` — importing the aggregate from the event file creates a fatal circular dependency.
6. Seven `AggregateRoot` methods throw "invoking method on object without retro events" on a freshly created (unpersisted) or snapshot-loaded aggregate: `clone`, `constructVersion`, `constructBefore`, `hasEventOfType`, `hasRetroEventOfType`, `getEventsOfType`, `getRetroEventsOfType`. Only `hasCurrentEventOfType` / `getCurrentEventsOfType` are always safe.
7. `AggregateStateFactory.create()` must be deterministic — no `Date.now()`, no id generation; the framework asserts two calls produce identical JSON. Spread `createDefaultAggregateState()` first; on a breaking state-shape change bump `typeVersion` after the spread and migrate old state in `update()` (bump via cast: `(state as { typeVersion: number }).typeVersion = 2`). Loading state whose `update()` output has a stale `typeVersion` throws.
8. Aggregate subclasses must keep the exact positional constructor `(domainContext, events, stateFactory, currentState?)` — `AggregateFactory`, `clone`, `constructVersion`, `constructBefore` all call it positionally. Don't write a custom constructor.
9. State fields must be primitives, arrays, plain JSON objects, or `Serializable`/`DomainObject` instances; any other object with `_`-prefixed fields throws at snapshot time.
10. `DomainEvent.apply()` is public but framework-internal — never call it; use the aggregate's protected `applyEvent(...)` from behavior methods. `event.aggregateId`/`id`/`userId` throw until the event has been applied.
11. `rebase` is protected: expose it by overriding with a public method that supplies your own rebased event; that event's `applyEvent` must call `AggregateStateHelper.rebaseState(state, defaultState, rebaseState, rebaseVersion)` with the three values the factory function receives, or the rebase silently does nothing.
12. `OrgAggregateStateFactory` takes an `OrgDomainContext` in its constructor — instantiate per request; never share across organizations. `OrgDomainEvent.apply` throws on organization mismatch.
13. Created events freeze the pristine `create()` defaults into `$frozenDefaultState`; on replay this overlays the base state so untouched fields come from the stream, not from a changed `create()`. Guard deliberate default changes with a test on `AggregateStateHelper.fingerprintState(new MyStateFactory().create())`.

## Reference implementation

- README.md — concepts, full API reference, best practices
- test/domain/ — complete working Todo aggregate (aggregate, state factory with typeVersion migrations, events, value object)
- test/domain.test.ts — executable spec: creation, replay, snapshots, reconstruction, cloning, rebasing

When docs and code disagree, trust test/domain/.
